title: Canonical scheme-chart transport through an etale commutative square
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $X,Y,X\prime,Y\prime$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ with their small etale sites [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\prime\to Y$, $h:X\prime\to X$, and $f\prime:X\prime\to Y\prime$ be morphisms, with $g$ and $h$ etale and $f\circ h=g\circ f\prime$. Use the scheme-chart categories $\mathcal A(f,V)$ [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. For $V\to Y\prime$ etale and a chart $q=(T\to X\prime,a:T\to V)$ of $\mathcal A(f\prime,V)$, define its base-change chart in $\mathcal A(f,gV)$ to have the same scheme $T$, chart map $T\to X\prime\xrightarrow{h}X$, and the same scheme map $a:T\to V$. Its commuting triangle over $Y$ is obtained from the chart triangle for $q$ and the commutative square. Here $gV$ denotes the same test scheme regarded over $Y$ by composition with $g$. This is the actual existing chart construction, defined for any commutative square with $g,h$ etale; no cartesian, surjectivity, finiteness or quasi-coherence condition is imposed.
